title: fix: flatten single-branch wildcard repetition to avoid ReDoS
body:
## Problem
GHSA-fc5q-39xc-vjpf describes nested unbounded repetition in single-branch extglobs such as `+(*a)`. The current guard handles ambiguous alternatives and nested extglobs, but ordinary wildcard tokens still produce nested quantifiers.

## Fix
For a single branch containing wildcard stars and only fixed-width text/qmark/bracket tokens, collapse the outer `+` repeat to one occurrence, or the outer `*` repeat to an optional occurrence. The branch language is closed under concatenation: earlier repetitions can be absorbed by a wildcard star. Preserve the already-parsed body, leading guard, escaping, path options and outer capture. Alternatives, slash/globstar/nested constructs, existing safety rewrites and explicit maxExtglobRecursion=false are unchanged. With capture:true the wildcard capture now covers the flattened body rather than the last repeat iteration; outer capture remains the full match.

## Verification
- Reproduced an unpatched +(*a) failing input exceeding an isolated 1-second deadline; patched version completes immediately.
- npm test: lint and all 2001 upstream tests pass.
- New hostile-input child-process deadlines and matching/escaping/capture cases.
- 22860 short-input true/false parity checks against npm 4.0.7 across default, dot, capture, Windows and bash options.

No application code, private data or credentials included. Offered as a focused patch for maintainer review, not a claim of an official published fix.
